<details>
The PKGBUILD defines variables, arrays, and functions in a standard way consistent with Arch Linux packaging practices. The top-level code consists only of variable assignments and a `for` loop that appends to the `source` array based on predefined sizes and URL patterns. This loop runs at sourcing time because it is in the global scope, but it only constructs source URLs using the package's own declared upstream (GitHub repository for satisfactorymodding/SatisfactoryModManager) and does not execute any external commands, perform downloads, or exfiltrate data.

There are no command substitutions, `curl`/`wget` calls, `eval` usage, or other dynamic code execution in the global scope. The `sha256sums` are provided and not set to `SKIP`, so checksum verification will occur later during build (though irrelevant for `makepkg --printsrcinfo`). The use of `declare -rg` and dynamic source array construction is valid shell scripting and within normal AUR packaging patterns. No malicious behavior can occur during sourcing.

Since `makepkg --printsrcinfo` only sources the PKGBUILD without executing build functions, and no harmful side effects occur during sourcing, this file is safe to process.
</details>
